deeperExplanation.question: What if the thought is important?
deeperExplanation.answer: Respond to an actual practical need. If you do not know the answer, ask a question. If the room is noisy, change the setting. A repeated prediction such as they will judge me is different from a concrete need you can address. You can hear it without opening another internal debate. The goal is selective response, not ignoring your mind or refusing to think about speech.

sections.narration:
Welcome. Today we are exploring Don’t Feed Every Speech Thought. The thought arrives: you will get stuck on the next word. You begin arguing with it, reassuring yourself and mentally testing a replacement. The thought is now the centre of the conversation.

In this session, we will notice a speech thought, separate noticing from following, and return to one meaningful action. I will explain the idea, show a visual example, and invite you to try it in a small experience of your own. You can ask me a question or switch to reading at any point. We will finish by choosing what, if anything, you want to take into a real conversation.

sections.narration: A thought can appear without receiving a full response. You are not required to prove it wrong before you speak. Today we will practise noticing a speech thought and leaving it unfinished while returning to the message. This is not suppression. Suppression says the thought must go. Non-reactivity says it can be here without becoming the task I work on.

sections.narration:
The thought arrives: you will get stuck on the next word. You begin arguing with it, reassuring yourself and mentally testing a replacement. The thought is now the centre of the conversation.

An unwanted prediction often asks for certainty. If you answer with another reassurance, it may ask again. Instead of winning an internal debate, choose something concrete in the present: the question you heard, the point you want to make or the person you are addressing. The prediction may remain in the background.

The goal is selective response, not ignoring your mind or refusing to think about speech.

sections.narration: Non-reactivity does not mean ignoring useful information or physical discomfort. You can respond to an actual need. We are reducing automatic engagement with repeated predictions, not refusing all thought. A changed, unchanged or uncertain experience is information, not a grade. You do not have to report relief for this attempt to count as exploration.

sections.narration: Try leaving one familiar reassurance loop unfinished during a low-pressure exchange. Note what you did next. During focused practice, you can deliberately explore this one tool. In an everyday conversation, give most of your attention to the message and the other person. A familiar support can be available if it helps; you do not have to monitor the tool throughout the exchange.
